messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging alert: kv-cache paging rate > 85% across prod-gpu-pool-3, observed from 18:37 UTC. Autoresolve disabled. Notified eng-runtime-oncall.

maria: I'm on it. seeing sustained p99 latency spikes on generation routes, also getting disk I/O saturation alerts from the node manager. kv cache resident size jumped from ~3.2GB -> ~12.7GB on several replicas.

ryan: Noted. Any deploys in the last hour?

maria: Yes — build 2026.3.14 applied a kernel-selection change for int8/awq that flips to int8-kernel-v2 for compatible models. Canary looked fine, but looks like when combined with the new continuous-batching tweak it blows up KV entries.

jia: Copy. Pulling logs.

jia: Logs show a pattern: for requests with long context (>=4096) the KV serializer picks dense layout and we ended up storing full attention tails uncompressed. snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T18:36:12Z model=redwood-awq-kv path=/v1/engines/gptx generate request_id=... kv_bytes=12563456 action=cache_put kernel=int8-kernel-v2
2026-03-15T18:36:13Z model=redwood-awq-kv path=/v1/engines/gptx generate request_id=... kv_bytes=12233444 action=cache_put kernel=int8-kernel-v2
```
So kv_bytes ~12MB per request, up from ~700KB baseline under fp16 kernel.

sam: ugh. that explains paging. If the allocator can't evict fast enough, we hit OOM/paging. Any immediate mitigations we can flip?

maria: Two-prong: 1) throttle continuous batching and force smaller batch window; 2) fallback kernel to fp16/int16 for affected model families. I'm pushing a hotfix config now.

ryan: How to toggle? command?\
jia: For batching: update route config -> {"continuous_batching": {"enabled": true, "max_batch_tokens": 2048, "window_ms": 50}}. Rapidly dropping max_batch_tokens from 8192 -> 2048 will reduce KV creation rate.

jia: Kernel fallback is a quick rollout: `rictl rollout --model gptx --kernel-policy force:fp16 --canary 10% --dry-run=false` (we use canary then ramp).

maria: I'm applying batching change to prod route /v1/engines/gptx now. ETA 90s.

oncall-bot: Deploy started (maria) 18:40:12 UTC — route-config update for /v1/engines/gptx.

maria: Config applied. Observability: KV insert rate droppped 60% within 30s, but a backlog of cached entries still causing high disk ops.

elaine: Can we also set a temporary per-pod kv_cache_limit to evict larger entries? we have a dynamic env var `KV_CACHE_MAX_ENTRY_BYTES` that we can set to 4MB to force early eviction.

kyle: I'm ready to roll the kernel fallback. Is there any risk to quality? minor degradation for a few tail cases, but better than paging.

maria: Launching kernel fallback canary to 10%. command executed.

oncall-bot: Rollout started (ryan) 18:42:05 UTC — rollout id rto-20260315-001, canary=10%.

ryan: Monitoring canary. preliminary metrics show canary replicas have normal kv_bytes ~800KB. Latency p99 for canary down to baseline.

jia: I'm running a quick script to identify pods with the largest KV footprints and evict entries older than 60s: 
```bash
for pod in $(kubectl get pods -l app=redwood-runtime -o name); do 
  kubectl exec $pod -- /bin/redwood-ctl kv-evict --older-than 60s --max-bytes 4MB;
done
```

logs: evicted ~1.3GB per pod on 6 pods.

maria: Good. Disk I/O dropping. Paging alerts fading.

oncall-bot: Incident metric: paging_rate(prod-gpu-pool-3) decreased from 91% -> 22% over 7 minutes.

sam: Customer impact assessment? which customers hit the worst?

jia: Early query: 5 enterprise customers had increased request latency (2-3x) for generate endpoints between 18:36-18:45 UTC. Two requests triggered 503s due to upstream timeouts, appears retriable. No data leaks.

elaine: Notifying Account Execs for those customers. Severity S2 for now.

maria: Post-mitigation steps: 1) finish kernel fallback ramp to 100% over 30m, 2) keep reduced batching window for one hour then test stepwise increase, 3) create revert patch on kernel-selector to only choose int8-kernel-v2 when model_sequence < 2048 and when `kv_shape==sparse` — that's the immediate model heuristic.

ryan: Agree. Also add telemetry that logs kv_bytes and kernel per request (sampled) to make future regressions easier to pinpoint. create ticket P-XXXX.

kyle: Quick note: AWQ-int8 variants have smaller model size on disk but due to new dense layout in v2 kernel we end up materializing larger KV. We'll follow-up with inference research to update kernel's on-disk layout heuristics.

ops-runbook-bot: Recommended runbook steps executed: fallback kernel canary, kv eviction script, reduce batching. Marking runbook step statuses: kernel_fallback=done, kv_eviction=done, batch_config_change=done.

maria: Handing off to eng-runtime for post-mortem and deeper root cause. oncall handoff: @ryan you have the next shift. I'll add context to the Jira and start the incident doc.

ryan: Taking handoff. I'll keep the rollout to 100% and run a mem-pressure soak for 45m. Leaving notes: we should add an automated guard that prevents kernel selection flips from enabling dense-KV layout unless `kv_bytes_sampling` < threshold.

sam: I'll own customer comms draft. ETA 30m for initial message.

elaine: Also schedule a sync with research + runtime tomorrow to discuss kernel heuristics and batching interplay.

maria: TL;DR: int8-kernel-v2 + recent continuous-batching increase produced large dense KV entries -> KV cache blowup -> disk paging -> latency increase + 503s. Mitigations: reduced batch token window, kernel fallback, targeted eviction; paging mitigated and customers largely unaffected after retries. Follow-ups: kernel selector guard, telemetry, runbook update, postmortem.

oncall-bot: Incident state: mitigated (18:58:00 UTC). Severity remains S2 pending postmortem.

ryan: Adding this thread to incident doc and closing handoff.

sam: Copy. drafting customer note now.

maria: Thanks everyone. Adding action items to P-XXXX and will assign owners.

kyle: FYI — I'll open a kernel-heuristics PR with a failing unit test that replicates dense-KV case.

ops-runbook-bot: Post-incident checklist queued: metrics retention increased for kv_bytes, add alert for per-model kv_bytes spike, add runbook step for kernel rollbacks.

maria: Closing thread for active mitigation; will reopen if paging returns. :white_check_mark:
